newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks climbed in late afternoon trade on Monday, bolstered by robust foreign interest which pushed them to end near the day's best levels.
Dealers said gains received further support from a strong showing on Wall Street on Friday, hopes of another rise on the Dow on Monday and local futures arbitrage activity.
"There was a lot of foreign money pouring in this afternoon. It came through London, but the source could be anywhere," one equity dealer said.
By the close the industrial 100 percent index had added 46.5 points to 8,285.6, hoisting the all-share index 58.9 points at 7,074.7.

Shares initially started the day firm, boosted by a 49-point gain on Wall Street on Friday, which smoothed some rattled nerves following the U.S. market's bloodletting earlier last week when it recorded its fourth-biggest loss in history.
Early strength was built on by arbitrage activity where investors sold off futures contracts in exchange for purchases of the cheaper underlying stocks.
Big industrial gainers on the day include Amic which put on 150 cents to 179 rand, Sasol which added 75 cents to 49.50 rand and Engen which lifed 25 cents or over one percent to 23.10 rand.
Engen released first half results after the close showing earnings up 21.6 percent to 107 cents, slightly above analysts' forecasts of a 103.2 cent rise.

The day was also characterised by a number of new listings, including two tourism groups, Tourvest TRTJ.J and Avis AVSJ.J, which both debuted strongly in busy trade. Avis ended at 695 cents, opening at 625, and Tourvest finished at 180 from a two rand opening trade.
Gold stocks, after a slow start, moved higher in the afternoon as bullion clambered above the $348 mark and in tandem with industrials' run, dealers said.
The gold index ended up 16.4 points at 1,307.9 with Vaal Reefs up 425 cents at 270.25 rand and Dries adding 95 cents to 41.25 rand.
Dealers differed on the overall market's possible path on Tuesday with some favouring consolidation at current levels and others looking to more upward movement amid expectations of a higher Dow.
"It looks like it could be strong once again tomorrow. Everything depends on what Nasdaq does and what the Dow does," said Dominick Rey, a trader at Investec Fergusson.
On the equity futures market contracts were firm in late trading, anticipating a better Wall Street on Monday amid gains on the U.S. S&P futures contract.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,085/95 from 8,038, the all-share at 6,501/08 from 6,458 and the gold contract at 910/20 from 904.
